questions.title: Woolf log-odds-ratio interval for a positive 2 by 2 table
questions.description: Focused integrated L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Woolf (1955). Let Y_1 and Y_0 be independent binomial counts from two fixed groups of sizes n_1 and n_0, with success probabilities p_1 and p_0 strictly between zero and one. Write the positive observed 2 by 2 cells as a=Y_1, b=n_1-Y_1, c=Y_0, and d=n_0-Y_0. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the maximum-likelihood log odds ratio log(ad/(bc)), its reciprocal-cell plug-in variance, and the two-sided 95 percent large-sample Wald interval on both log and odds-ratio scales from the joint binomial CLT and delta method. Make the score/likelihood or invariance argument for the estimator, the gradient calculation, Slutsky step, consistency conditions, pointwise coverage claim, group-swap and outcome-complement transformations, and all positivity and increasing-information assumptions explicit. Explain why zero or sparse cells, dependent or matched observations, stratification, exact conditional inference, continuity corrections, and finite-sample coverage are outside this result. Do not claim an exact interval, rare-event validity, causal interpretation, risk-ratio identity, source replication, novelty, or formal proof. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_woolf_log_odds_ratio_interval and must implement the exact frozen run_estimator(request) contract. Exploratory Python or R may check likelihood identities, delta-method scaling, label transformations, and simulated coverage. A separately frozen confirmatory evaluator uses fresh independent-binomial tables, evaluator-owned seeds and configurations fixed before outcomes, and at least 5000 independent replicates per design. It checks exact executable identities, standardized log-estimator behavior, variance calibration, and interval coverage with Monte Carlo uncertainty. These finite experiments test one implementation on frozen interior-probability configurations and do not prove asymptotic normality or coverage. Source replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable. Every unresolved mathematical, executable, empirical, or scope gap must remain explicit.

request_fields.name: group_1_successes
request_fields.meaning: The positive success-cell count a in group 1.
request_fields.indexing: Forms group-1 total n_1=a+b with group_1_failures.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, floating, string, null, array, object, zero, negative, and values above 1000000 rather than coercing, rounding, clipping, or adding a continuity correction.

request_fields.name: group_1_failures
request_fields.meaning: The positive failure-cell count b in group 1.
request_fields.indexing: Forms group-1 total n_1=a+b with group_1_successes.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, floating, string, null, array, object, zero, negative, and values above 1000000 rather than coercing, rounding, clipping, or adding a continuity correction.

request_fields.name: group_0_successes
request_fields.meaning: The positive success-cell count c in group 0.
request_fields.indexing: Forms group-0 total n_0=c+d with group_0_failures.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, floating, string, null, array, object, zero, negative, and values above 1000000 rather than coercing, rounding, clipping, or adding a continuity correction.

request_fields.name: group_0_failures
request_fields.meaning: The positive failure-cell count d in group 0.
request_fields.indexing: Forms group-0 total n_0=c+d with group_0_successes.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject Boolean, floating, string, null, array, object, zero, negative, and values above 1000000 rather than coercing, rounding, clipping, or adding a continuity correction.

response_fields.name: log_odds_ratio
response_fields.indexing: Group 1 relative to group 0, success relative to failure.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not reverse either group or outcome orientation.

response_fields.name: odds_ratio
response_fields.indexing: Group 1 relative to group 0, success relative to failure.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not return a risk ratio, odds difference, reciprocal orientation, or continuity-corrected estimate.

response_fields.name: asymptotic_variance
response_fields.meaning: The reciprocal-cell plug-in variance estimate for log_odds_ratio.
response_fields.indexing: One scalar using all four cells once.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not use an odds-ratio-scale variance, pooled-null variance, continuity correction, or omit a cell.

response_fields.name: standard_error
response_fields.meaning: The positive square root of asymptotic_variance.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not return the variance itself or an odds-ratio-scale standard error.

response_fields.name: ci_lower_log
response_fields.meaning: The lower endpoint of the two-sided 95 percent large-sample Wald interval for the log odds ratio.
response_fields.shape: One finite non-Boolean scalar strictly below ci_upper_log.
response_fields.indexing: Lower endpoint for group 1 relative to group 0.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not clip at zero, use a one-sided quantile, or claim exact finite-sample coverage.

response_fields.name: ci_upper_log
response_fields.meaning: The upper endpoint of the two-sided 95 percent large-sample Wald interval for the log odds ratio.
response_fields.shape: One finite non-Boolean scalar strictly above ci_lower_log.
response_fields.indexing: Upper endpoint for group 1 relative to group 0.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not clip, use a one-sided quantile, or claim exact finite-sample coverage.

response_fields.name: ci_lower_odds_ratio
response_fields.meaning: The lower positive endpoint obtained by exponentiating ci_lower_log.
response_fields.shape: One finite positive non-Boolean scalar strictly below ci_upper_odds_ratio.
response_fields.indexing: Lower endpoint for group 1 relative to group 0.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not exponentiate a standard error or construct a symmetric interval on the odds-ratio scale.

response_fields.name: ci_upper_odds_ratio
response_fields.meaning: The upper positive endpoint obtained by exponentiating ci_upper_log.
response_fields.shape: One finite positive non-Boolean scalar strictly above ci_lower_odds_ratio.
response_fields.indexing: Upper endpoint for group 1 relative to group 0.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not exponentiate a standard error or construct a symmetric interval on the odds-ratio scale.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly the four declared fields and the response exactly the eight declared fields. Missing, extra, malformed, coercible-only, nonpositive, or out-of-domain values are rejected.

Every returned value follows from log(ad/(bc)), exp of that estimate, V=1/a+1/b+1/c+1/d, sqrt(V), and log-scale endpoints at plus or minus 1.959963984540054 standard errors with exponentiated odds-ratio endpoints.

Swapping the complete group-1 and group-0 rows negates log_odds_ratio and both log interval endpoints with their order reversed, reciprocates odds_ratio and both odds-ratio interval endpoints with their order reversed, and leaves asymptotic_variance and standard_error unchanged.
Swapping successes with failures within both groups has the same sign, reciprocal, reversed-endpoint, variance, and standard-error transformations as swapping the groups.

Multiplying all four counts by the same valid positive integer leaves both point estimates unchanged, divides asymptotic_variance by that integer, divides standard_error and each log-scale half-width by its square root, and recomputes the odds-ratio endpoints by exponentiation.
Repeated calls with the same request return the same JSON value and do not mutate the request, use random state, read files, invoke subprocesses, or use the network.

empirical_claims.meaning: For every frozen positive table, the candidate is compared with an independent exact implementation of all eight returned Woolf objects.

Across fresh independent-binomial tables with interior probabilities, the centered log_odds_ratio divided by its reported standard_error is checked for approximately zero mean and unit second moment using predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty.
The empirical variance of log_odds_ratio and the mean reported asymptotic_variance are compared under each frozen design with a predeclared relative-error bound.

Coverage of the true log odds ratio by the reported two-sided 95 percent log interval, equivalently coverage of the true odds ratio by the exponentiated interval, is compared with 0.95 using predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty.
Group sizes, success probabilities, seeds, at least 5000 independent replicates per design, summaries, and acceptance bounds are evaluator-owned and frozen before the product run.

The experiment assesses one implementation under finitely many independent-binomial, interior-probability configurations with positive realized cells. It is not proof and does not validate exact finite-sample coverage, zero or sparse cells, dependent or matched observations, stratification, continuity corrections, causal interpretation, source replication, novelty, or formal closure.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: For every valid bounded request, run_estimator performs finite scalar arithmetic and returns exactly one response without optimization, randomization, file access, network access, subprocesses, or request mutation.
